rankings.title: Delivery performance
rankings.intro: How infrastructure projects held to their budgets and their timetables. Every figure below is derived from the contract terms and cost figures recorded on each section, and a section only appears once the data supports the claim.
rankings.coverage: Measured on {lots} sections: {estimate} with an estimate-to-outturn comparison, {award} against the contract award, {completedSlip} delivered with a contract timetable, {ongoingSlip} still running.
rankings.coverageGap: The gaps are missing data, not clean records — sections without a recorded outturn cost or contracted duration cannot be measured and are left out rather than assumed on budget.
rankings.basisEstimateHelp: Pre-tender estimate compared with the final outturn cost. Captures everything that happened in between, scope changes included.
rankings.basisAwardHelp: The signed contract value compared with the final outturn cost — what the contractor bid against what the public paid.
rankings.slipIntro: Measured against the date each contract implied: construction start (or the award, where the start is unknown) plus the contracted design and execution months.
rankings.slipInProgressHelp: Compared against the announced opening where one exists, otherwise against today. Sections not yet past their contract date are excluded.
rankings.bestIntro: Sections delivered on or ahead of the date their contract implied, and those that came in under budget.
rankings.byContractorIntro: Builders only — a construction overrun belongs to whoever built the thing. Joint-venture work counts toward each partner, and name variants are resolved to one firm. Shown for firms with at least {min} measured sections.
rankings.emptyOverrunEstimate: No section yet records both an estimate and a final outturn cost. Backfill cost.estimated and cost.actual to populate this table.
rankings.emptyOverrunAward: No section yet records both a contract value and a final outturn cost. Backfill contract.value and cost.actual to populate this table.
rankings.emptySlip: No section yet records both a contracted duration and an anchor date.
rankings.methodologyCosts: Costs carry the price year they were quoted in, and both sides of every comparison are restated into a common year before the percentage is taken — an estimate made in 2013 is never measured directly against money spent in 2023. The nominal figure is shown alongside so the inflation component is visible. Costs in different currencies are not compared, because no exchange rates are held.
rankings.methodologySchedule: Schedule slip uses the contract as the baseline rather than a press announcement, because that is the commitment the public paid for and the only baseline present for sections whose announced dates were never recorded. Negative values mean early.
rankings.leagueNote: Sorted by median slip, worst first.
rankings.emptyOnTime: No measured section has yet been delivered on or ahead of its contract date.
rankings.emptyUnderBudget: No measured section has yet come in at or under budget.
